items.requirement: Identify the review as a mixed-methods review protocol.
items.prompt: What is the mixed-methods review title and why does it require both quantitative and qualitative evidence?
items.helpText: The title should signal the mixed-methods nature of the synthesis.
items.exampleResponse: Mixed-methods review protocol: effectiveness and acceptability of community-based diabetes self-management interventions.

items.prompt: Why must quantitative and qualitative evidence be integrated for this question?
items.helpText: Explain what each evidence stream contributes and why integration matters.
items.exampleResponse: Effect estimates will show whether interventions work, while qualitative evidence will explain acceptability and implementation conditions.

items.requirement: State quantitative, qualitative, and integrated questions.
items.prompt: What are the quantitative question, qualitative question, and integrated mixed-methods question?
items.helpText: Avoid a mismatch between the questions and the planned integration method.
items.exampleResponse: Quantitative: What is the effect on HbA1c? Qualitative: What shapes acceptability? Integrated: Which intervention features appear effective and acceptable?

items.requirement: Specify eligibility for quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies.
items.prompt: Which study designs and evidence components will be eligible for each evidence stream?
items.helpText: Clarify how mixed-methods primary studies will be separated or integrated.
items.exampleResponse: We will include randomized, quasi-experimental, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies with extractable quantitative or qualitative data.

items.prompt: What quantitative and qualitative data will be extracted, and will any data transformation be performed?
items.helpText: JBI mixed-methods guidance often distinguishes convergent integrated and convergent segregated approaches.
items.exampleResponse: Effect estimates and qualitative findings will be extracted separately; qualitative findings may be configured with quantitative result categories during integration.

items.prompt: Which tools will appraise quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods evidence?
items.helpText: Use design-appropriate tools and state how appraisal affects synthesis.
items.exampleResponse: Randomized studies will use RoB 2, qualitative studies CASP, and mixed-methods studies MMAT.

items.prompt: Will synthesis be convergent integrated, convergent segregated, or sequential, and how will findings be integrated?
items.helpText: Name the integration method, not just the individual synthesis methods.
items.exampleResponse: We will use a convergent segregated design, synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence separately, then integrate through a joint display.

items.requirement: Plan certainty or confidence assessment for integrated findings.
items.prompt: How will certainty, confidence, or credibility be judged across the integrated evidence?
items.helpText: Consider GRADE for quantitative findings and CERQual for qualitative findings.
items.exampleResponse: GRADE and CERQual assessments will be presented alongside integrated findings in a joint display.
